name: Terror
label: Victory Records
lede: Scott Vogel quit music, moved from Buffalo to Los Angeles, and took a call from the members of Carry On who had regrouped. By the band's own count, Terror has played more than 3,000 shows since.

eras.title: Quitting, and a call from Carry On
eras.text: Scott Vogel had sung in Slugfest, Despair and Buried Alive, the last of them on Victory Records. He quit, moved west, and within months Los Angeles hardcore had handed him a new band.

years.h: Scott Vogel turns down 100 Demons and leaves for Los Angeles
years.p: Slugfest, Despair and Buried Alive were behind him. Vogel told Kerrang he moved west intending to leave music, and an offer to sing for 100 Demons didn't change that.
years.xp:
Buried Alive had been on Victory Records, with The Death of Your Perfect World in 1999 and Last Rites in 2001. Vogel has described himself in those years as someone who only cared about hardcore and pushed everyone around him.

Then Carry On, the Los Angeles band a friend had played him, broke up and its members regrouped. They called and asked him to sing, and he said yes after seeing them play.

years.h: Carry On breaks up and Terror starts with its guitarist
years.p: Vogel sings, ex-Carry On guitarist Todd Jones plays guitar, Nick Jett drums and Matt Smith plays bass. The name Terror comes in April, after the first shows are already booked.

years.h: Terror's first show opens for Diehard Youth in a Ventura warehouse
years.p: The date is April 26 at Pat's Warehouse, a warm-up. By May 15-19 Terror is opening West Coast dates for Death Threat, American Nightmare and Striking Distance.

years.h: Terror grows to five and spends the fall with Eighteen Visions
years.p: Richard Thurston joins on bass. The band has two demos behind it, 4 Song Demo and Don't Need Your Help.

years.h: Carl Schwartz takes over bass from Richard Thurston
years.p: Schwartz holds the job through the end of 2005.

yt: Vogel with Biohazard, Hold My Own, Hellfest 2003
years.h: Lowest of the Low arrives on Bridge 9, then Europe with Biohazard
years.p: Terror's first EP comes out on Boston's Bridge 9, with the live album Life & Death alongside it. The spring tour of Europe is with Biohazard and Caliban.
years.xp: Vogel also guested with Biohazard that year, singing Hold My Own at Hellfest. Terror spent the summer with Most Precious Blood and the fall touring with Every Time I Die.

eras.title: Sounds of the Underground and a bad back
eras.text: The debut album sold over 40,000 copies and put Terror on tours with Lamb of God and Hatebreed. Vogel's spine started to complain, and the founding guitarist moved on.

years.src: Wikipedia: Terror · Wikipedia: One with the Underdogs
years.h: Debut album One with the Underdogs clears 40,000 copies
years.p: Recorded at Sound City in Van Nuys and produced by the band for Trustkill, with Jamey Jasta of Hatebreed and Freddy Cricien of Madball guesting. It reaches number 28 on Independent Albums.

years.h: Disc trouble in Scott Vogel's neck and back cancels shows
years.p: Several dates go in late 2004. By November Vogel is back, co-headlining the US with [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]].

years.h: Terror rides Sounds of the Underground with Lamb of God
years.p: The traveling metal and hardcore package also carries Unearth and [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]]. Terror then headlines North America with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]] in support.
years.xp: Terror also supported Converge on its Canadian fall tour that year.

years.h: Carl Schwartz leaves for First Blood
years.p: He quits to play there full-time. Jonathan Buske takes over bass in March 2006.

years.cap: Terror live in Wolverhampton, UK, December 2006
years.h: Leeway's Eddie Sutton guests on Always the Hard Way
years.p: Zeuss produces at Planet Z in Massachusetts, and the rappers Murs and Mr. Dibbs take an interlude. The album reaches number 10 on Heatseekers.
years.xp:
Sutton sings on So Close to Defeat. The album also reached 19 on Top Independent Albums.

Terror spent the summer on Sounds of the Underground with As I Lay Dying, In Flames and Trivium, and made its first Persistence tour run with [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: Todd Jones starts Nails and fronts it
years.p: The man who founded Terror with Scott Vogel forms the grind-heavy [[Nails|a7d9c5f6-751d-4ea5-bf6d-39f1751d44a1]], playing guitar and singing.

years.h: The Damned, the Shamed moves Terror to Century Media
years.p: The third album comes out May 26. Bassist Jonathan Buske leaves in September.
years.xp: Wikipedia's summary has AllMusic calling it "solid" and "a CD that isn't big on originality but definitely comes through in terms of quality." Terror also released the live album CBGB OMFUG Masters, recorded June 10, 2004.

eras.title: A new guitarist, a new bassist, no days off
eras.text: Terror kept touring across Asia, Australia and Europe. The line-up that settled here would make the next three albums together.

years.h: Jordan Posner fills in for Doug Weber and never leaves
years.p: Weber leaves in January 2009. Posner steps in on guitar as a temporary fix and stays for good, and David Wood takes over bass the same year.

years.h: Keepers of the Faith lands on Century Media
years.p: Terror's fourth album is out November 10 and sells about 2,500 in week one. Bridge 9 releases No Regrets, No Shame the same year, filmed at the Showcase Theater in Corona, California in 2003.
years.xp: Scenepoint Blank wrote that Terror had "reclaimed the crown of modern hardcore."

years.h: Terror headlines Hell on Earth, then Rebellion
years.p: Every Time I Die and All Shall Perish support on Hell on Earth. [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and Death Before Dishonor join Rebellion.

years.h: Terror pulls a Czech show for Randy Blythe
years.p: On the Persistence Tour, Terror cancels its Czech Republic date in support of Lamb of God singer Randy Blythe, then facing a manslaughter case in Prague.

eras.title: Victory Records, and Vogel's back gives out twice
eras.text: Terror signed to the label that had released Vogel's Buried Alive more than a decade earlier. Live by the Code became the band's only Billboard 200 entry, and then the injuries came.

years.h: Terror signs with Victory, Vogel's old Buried Alive label
years.p: Victory takes Terror's CDs from January 15. Reaper Records does the vinyl.

years.cap: Terror at With Full Force Festival, Germany, 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Live by the Code · Wikipedia: Terror
years.h: Chad Gilbert of New Found Glory produces Live by the Code
years.p: Eleven songs in under 27 minutes. It enters the Billboard 200 at 145 with about 3,200 sold, Terror's only appearance on that chart, and tops Heatseekers.
years.xp:
Vogel described it as the band's dirtiest, most hardcore record since its early releases. The line-up was Vogel, Jordan Posner, Martin Stewart, David Wood and Nick Jett.

AllMusic, as quoted on Wikipedia, praised its "furious lyrics and chunky guitar lines." Six songs got videos, from Live by the Code to Cold Truth.

years.cap: Scott Vogel at Paaspop, Netherlands, April 2014
years.h: Terror and Suicidal Tendencies co-headline Persistence
years.p: Terror also plays the Vans Warped Tour and tours with Stick to Your Guns and Hundredth.
years.xp: Terror's own Defiant Music label reissued the first three records, Lowest of the Low, One with the Underdogs and Always the Hard Way. The live album Live in Seattle came out the same year.

years.h: Ben Cook produces The 25th Hour, Terror's second for Victory
years.p: Paul Miner records it in January 2015, 14 songs in under 23 minutes. It reaches 8 on Top Hard Rock Albums and 46 in Germany.
years.xp:
Andrew Kline of [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] was among the gang vocalists. Blabbermouth's Ray Van Horn scored it 8.5 out of 10.

In June a disc injury in Vogel's back cancelled the band's immediate tour plans. They were back out in the fall with [[Code Orange|b87d5807-c37a-4d0e-a53c-9cdf6bc6caa1]].

years.h: A second spinal injury pulls Terror off The Life & Death Tour
years.p: Terror is headlining with Power Trip and Harm's Way when Scott Vogel is hurt again. He needs back surgery, and the band scraps every upcoming date.

eras.title: Todd Jones comes back
eras.text: A new bassist, a new label, and then a surprise: Jones, the founding guitarist who had left to start Nails, returned to produce. The pandemic made it Vogel and Jones alone in the studio.

years.cap: Terror at Reload Festival, Germany, August 2017
years.h: Cruel Hand's Chris Linkovich fills in on bass, then stays
years.p: He starts filling in for David Wood in April, and by June he's the bassist. The same year Terror moves to Pure Noise with the EP The Walls Will Fall.
years.xp: Blabbermouth called The Walls Will Fall "a notable return to form."

years.h: Will Putney produces Total Retaliation
years.p: Terror's first Pure Noise album reaches 12 on Independent Albums. A headlining run with Harm's Way, Backtrack and Year of the Knife follows.
years.xp: The single Total Demolition came out August 9. Exclaim! found the album "most rewarding in small doses," while Blabbermouth said Terror were "at the top of the pack."

years.h: Sink to the Hell drops with no warning
years.p: Four lost and unreleased Terror songs arrive on War Records.

years.h: Todd Jones is back, producing and playing on Trapped in a World
years.p: Terror re-records songs from across its career for Good Fight, live in the studio. Jones, the founding guitarist, produces and plays guitar.
years.xp: Jones kept the production job for the next album, Pain Into Power.

years.h: A UFC light heavyweight sings Out of My Face with Terror
years.p: Khalil Rountree Jr. joins the band onstage at a California show and calls Terror a Hall of Fame hardcore band.
years.xp: Rountree said Terror's lyrics and messages had helped him through difficult times.

years.big: "I turned my Instagram off. I swear to God, the lyrics started pouring out of me."
years.src: Kerrang · Wikipedia: Terror · Wikipedia: Scott Vogel
years.h: Scott Vogel quits Instagram and writes Pain Into Power
years.p: Vogel told Kerrang he had been stuck on lyrics until he logged off. He wrote six songs in two weeks, and Todd Jones produced while the pandemic kept the other members out of the studio.
years.xp:
Released May 6 on Pure Noise, it reached number 8 on the German albums chart. Metal Injection gave it 9 out of 10 and called it "relentless, bone-snapping stuff."

The same year Vogel moved back home to Buffalo after two decades in Los Angeles.

eras.title: Still suffering, still touring
eras.text: Two decades in, Terror kept playing everywhere from Australia to Japan, Vogel picked up a best-vocalist ranking, and Jones produced another album.

years.h: Hatebreed's Rise of Brutality anniversary tour brings Terror along
years.p: Terror joins [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s 20th anniversary run for The Rise of Brutality. Most of the year is US shows, plus select dates in Europe.

years.cap: Terror at Full Rewind Summer Open Air, Roitzschjora, Germany, August 2024
q: I was a jock and I still am a jock.
years.h: Alternative Press puts Scott Vogel second among hardcore vocalists
years.p: Terror's year runs from Australia with Kublai Khan to Europe in spring and summer and a short run in Japan.
years.xp: Vogel grew up in the Buffalo suburbs and still describes himself as a sports guy first. His step-brother brought home Run-D.M.C., punk and New York hardcore.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits and Death Before Dishonor share a European bill with Terror
years.p: The fall tour comes with the news that the ninth album, Still Suffer, is set for 2026 on Flatspot Records.

years.h: A 20-minute film follows Terror through Latin America
years.p: A Deeper Struggle, directed by Derek Rathbun, comes out April 23, the day before the new album.

years.h: Still Suffer is Terror's first album on Flatspot
years.p: Todd Jones produces and Jon Markson mixes. It reaches 31 in Germany, and Terror tours North America with Pain of Truth and joins Hatebreed on Summer Slaughter.
